# Golden snapshot fixtures

Four images chosen to fail in different ways. See `core/tests/golden.rs`.

| file | source | licence |
|---|---|---|
| `portrait.png` | Commodore Grace M. Hopper, USN, by James S. Davis | **Public domain** - a work of the US Federal Government |
| `logo.png` | the shell's own `src/assets/hero.png` | this project |
| `gradient.png` | generated by `gen.py` | this project |
| `screenshot.png` | generated by `gen.py` | this project |

The portrait is a real photograph on purpose. A synthetic face cannot tell you
whether the quantiser produces something recognisable or mush, which is the
only question these snapshots exist to answer.

## Looking at a snapshot

The snapshots are ANSI, so `cat` renders them in colour in a terminal. Where
that is not possible - a review, a tool boundary - render one to PNG with the
board's own font and palette:

```bash
python3 core/tests/fixtures/ansi2png.py \
  core/tests/snapshots/golden__portrait_is_a_recognisable_face.snap /tmp/out.png
```

**Never accept a snapshot without looking at it.** An accepted snapshot is a
claim that the output is good; an unexamined one defends mush forever, failing
loudly the day someone improves the quantiser and passing silently every day it
stays bad.
